newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firmer in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firmer in thin trading.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds firmed on Tuesday, with prices stabilising at new levels after last week's rise, but dealers said trading was thin following the U.S. President's Day holiday on Monday.
"Prices have been fluctuating by just 0.20 points, but it is all calm as trading will start later in the U.S. after the holiday," Avtobank dealer Alla Zakharova said.
"Besides, the market seems to be pausing for breath after the rise last week," she added.
Dealers said the two longest tranches traded actively and rose most. Local demand for the 2008 maturity was balanced by paper coming from London, they added.

"No clear trend is seen now. Spreads remain tiny (0.10-0.15 points). The market must be standing on the levels it is unable to go through at the moment, but it will not go down as there is strong support," an International Moscow Bank dealer said.
The most liquid third, fourth and fifth tranches were finding support at 87.00, 64.00 and 45.00, respectively.
